title: AI-Ops, Autonomous Remediation & GPU Inference Workloads
summary: Schedule GPU workloads (`nvidia.com/gpu`) with taints/tolerations, deploy distributed LLM inference services (vLLM), and run AI-Ops automated root-cause analysis and self-healing.
learningObjectives: Schedule GPU-accelerated LLM inference pods onto tainted NVIDIA GPU worker nodes.
Execute AI-Ops diagnostic analysis (`aiops analyze`) to pinpoint cluster anomalies.
Trigger policy-guarded autonomous remediation (`aiops remediate`) and verify cluster recovery.

curriculumModules.title: Kubernetes GPU Scheduling, Device Plugins & Taints/Tolerations
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: GPU worker nodes run the NVIDIA Device Plugin exposing `nvidia.com/gpu` allocatable capacity and are tainted (`nvidia.com/gpu=present:NoSchedule`) so CPU-only pods do not waste expensive accelerators.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Configure LLM inference deployments (vLLM, Triton) with explicit `limits: { "nvidia.com/gpu": 1 }` and a matching `NoSchedule` toleration.

curriculumModules.title: AI-Ops Root-Cause Analysis (K8sGPT) & Autonomous Self-Healing
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: AI-Ops controllers correlate Kubernetes Events, Prometheus metrics, and pod statuses to synthesize human-readable Root-Cause Analysis (RCA) and execute policy-approved remediations.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Run continuous AI-Ops analyzers (`aiops analyze`) with human-in-the-loop or GitOps-guarded `aiops remediate` actions.

labs.title: Scheduling LLM Inference Workloads onto Tainted GPU Nodes
labs.scenario: Deployment `vllm-inference` in `production` requests `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` and is stuck `Pending` because node `kubelabs-worker-gpu-02` has taint `nvidia.com/gpu=present:NoSchedule`. Add the required toleration so the LLM pod schedules and runs.
labs.productionContext: GPU node pools are always tainted in production to prevent general web workloads from consuming $30/hr GPU instances.
objectives: Patch `deployment/vllm-inference` in `production` to add a toleration for key `nvidia.com/gpu`
Verify `vllm-inference` pod transitions from `Pending` to `Running` on `kubelabs-worker-gpu-02`
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: vllm-inference
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: vllm-inference
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: vllm-inference
    spec:
      tolerations:
        - key: nvidia.com/gpu
          operator: Exists
          effect: NoSchedule
      containers:
        - name: vllm
          image: ghcr.io/kubelabs/vllm-openai:v0.6.3
          resources:
            limits:
              nvidia.com/gpu: 1

steps.title: Observe Pending GPU Pod
steps.instruction: Run `kubectl get pods -n production` to see `vllm-inference` stuck `Pending` (`Unschedulable`).

validationRules.description: Pod for production/vllm-inference is Running on GPU worker node
validationRules.name: vllm-inference
validationRules.remediation: Ensure vllm-inference pod transitions to Running.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Verify with `kubectl get pods -n production` that `vllm-inference` is `Running` on `kubelabs-worker-gpu-02`.

labs.title: AI-Ops Automated Root-Cause Analysis & Self-Healing
labs.scenario: A broken deployment (`anomaly-detector`) in `production` is failing in `ImagePullBackOff`. Run `aiops analyze` to diagnose the anomaly and `aiops remediate` to trigger autonomous remediation.
labs.productionContext: AI-Ops agents accelerate incident triage by correlating pod faults and executing pre-approved remediation runbooks.
objectives: Run `aiops analyze` to generate an automated Root-Cause Analysis report
Run `aiops remediate` to heal the broken deployment and record `monitoring/aiops-remediation-report`
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: aiops-remediation-report
  namespace: monitoring
data:
  status: remediated

steps.title: Run AI-Ops Root-Cause Analysis
steps.instruction: Execute `aiops analyze` to inspect cluster anomalies.

steps.title: Trigger Autonomous Remediation
steps.instruction: Execute `aiops remediate` to heal the broken image and record the remediation report.

validationRules.description: Pods for production/anomaly-detector healed and Running
validationRules.name: anomaly-detector

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Run `aiops analyze` followed by `aiops remediate` and verify `kubectl get pods -n production`.

assessmentQuestions.question: Why are Kubernetes GPU worker nodes tainted with `nvidia.com/gpu=present:NoSchedule` in production?
options: To prevent general CPU-only workloads from scheduling onto expensive GPU nodes and starving ML/LLM workloads
To disable container networking on GPU nodes
Because kube-scheduler cannot schedule more than 1 pod per cluster without a taint
To force containers to run in privileged mode
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Tainting GPU nodes with `NoSchedule` ensures only Pods that explicitly declare a matching `toleration` (such as ML training or LLM inference pods) can be placed on GPU hardware.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the safest architectural pattern for deploying autonomous AI-Ops remediation in production?
options: Granting an unconstrained LLM raw root SSH access to all production database servers
Policy-guarded remediation where AI-Ops diagnostics propose or trigger bounded, declarative controller/GitOps actions audited by RBAC and admission policies
Turning off Prometheus alerts and letting AI guess when outages happen
Deleting any namespace that emits a warning event
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Production AI-Ops combines deterministic telemetry correlation with bounded, RBAC-scoped, policy-validated remediation actions.
